newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS TAKE IT EASY BUT BEAT FENERBAHCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS TAKE IT EASY BUT BEAT FENERBAHCE.

text.p: Holders Juventus, already through to the European Cup quarter-finals, dashed Fenerbahce's hopes of joining them by beating the Turks 2-0 in their final Champions' League Group C match on Wednesday.

The Italians, whose place as group leaders was also untouchable, took the lead just before halftime when striker Michele Padovano crashed in a header in the 41st minute from a well-placed cross from Mark Iuliano on the left wing.

Fenerbahce, who needed an unlikely win in the Delle Alpi stadium to be sure of going through, took the match to the home team in the early minutes and were unlucky not to score through Nigerians Uche Okechekwu and Augustine Okocha.

Okechekwu hit the crossbar with a bouncing header in the 17th minute while Okocha had a second-half shot deflected around the upright. Nicola Amoruso, who replaced Alessandro del Piero at halftime, made it 2-0 six minutes from time.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi was deliberately cautious, resting tired players and those in danger of picking up a second booking and thereby missing key matches.
Croat Alen Boksic was left on the bench along with key defender Ciro Ferrara, while injured French midfielder Didier Deschamps and Yugoslav Vladimir Jugovic watched from the stands.

Neither of the two goals produced the biggest roar of the night. That was reserved for news -- delivered twice -- that Norway's Rosenborg were beating AC Milan in another Champions' League encounter in Milan.
Rosenborg's win knocked Milan out and prevented a Juventus-Milan clash in the last eight.
"If a team can win in Milan on a special night like that then they are really strong." commented Lippi on quarter-final opponents Rosenborg.
"I don't deny that Milan-Juventus would have had a particular attraction but we now face a truly dangerous opponent, both technically and in spirit."
Sebastiao Lazaroni, the Brazilian coach of Fenerbahce, said his men had looked dangerous at times but had been unable to focus their attacks.

"However we go out with our heads high because we played some good football," he said of a team which had earlier in the tournament dealt Manchester United their first home defeat in European competition in 40 years.
Wednesday's result left Juventus on 16 points, ahead of Manchester United on nine and Fenerbahce on seven.
